title: Continuous Integration
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of continuous integration and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply automated test execution in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Continuous Integration is part of Debugging, Testing, and Software Quality. Start with automated test execution and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: External integrations fail in ordinary ways: invalid inputs, credentials, timeouts, status errors and schema changes must be handled explicitly.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: External integrations fail in ordinary ways: invalid inputs, credentials, timeouts, status errors and schema changes must be handled explicitly. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Sketch a least-privilege workflow with input validation, timeout/status checks and resource cleanup; do not use production credentials. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.limitations: Never use production credentials; this course does not execute network or database calls. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For continuous integration, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming external services always return valid data.
common_mistakes.why: Timeouts, authorization failures, rate limits and schema changes are normal failure cases.
common_mistakes.fix: Add timeouts, status/schema validation, least-privilege access and bounded retries.

common_mistakes.problem: Embedding credentials or sensitive rows in examples or logs.
common_mistakes.why: Secrets and private data can leak through source control or diagnostic output.
common_mistakes.fix: Use environment-based secret handling and synthetic examples; redact logs.

common_mistakes.problem: Leaving resources open after an error.
common_mistakes.why: Unclosed connections and files can leak resources or lock outputs.
common_mistakes.fix: Use reliable cleanup patterns and test both success and failure paths.
